translation.english_text: (Courtesan's house. Paranthaman waits for the courtesan to arrive. She comes and stands behind a curtain.)

Hey, come here! Take the money! (He takes a one-rupee coin and throws it.) Won't you take it! Are you coming, or shall I come? (He rises and comes forward.) Queen of love! Ornamental divine form of the mansion of beauty! O picture that cannot be erased and redrawn!
notes: The source utterance crosses PDF 87→88. The unusual 'அழித்தெழுதாச் சித்திரமே' reading is preserved distinctly from the following voice's 'அழுத்தெழுதாச் சித்திரமே'.

translation.english_text: O picture that cannot be overwritten! O swaying golden lamp! O pearl-like beauty! O eye-catching gem!
notes: The exact source speaker label remains 'Voice'. The printed variation 'அழுத்தெழுதாச்' is not normalized to Paranthaman's preceding 'அழித்தெழுதாச்'.

translation.english_text: Ah! Who? (Bama reveals herself.)
Ah! Bama!

It is I! You described me as the queen of love—look at that queen now in the guise of a courtesan! The ornamental divine form of the mansion of beauty—look at it shrivelled, fallen and disfigured in the shadow of society's crumbling little wall! The picture that could not be erased and redrawn—look at it corrected and rewritten every day by new connoisseurs of painting who pass through here, then left ruined in the street! The swaying golden lamp—look at it caught in the hands of the men who seek it every day and extinguished! The pearl-like beauty—look at it scorched while still a bud! The eye-catching gem—look at it lying covered in dirt! Wretch! Destroyer! Poet of love who once spoke poetry! Look... look... look... look!
Bama, wait! Forget what happened!
Forget? My honour itself is gone, you great sinner!
You yourself are the reason you lost your honour!....

Yes. In your palace of love, on the golden-jewelled bed, in the pleasure pavilion, singing graceful songs, you kept me day and night as an incomparable goddess of love. I alone leapt with a splash into the sewer of humiliation and turned into stone! Isn't that what happened!
It was all fate's game!
Fate!
Yes, fate! A strange parachute! Once you hold on to it, you must land wherever it brings you down!
Only those who board the aeroplane called ignorance need that parachute! I was the fool who boarded it! I was the fool!
You haven't read the old shastras.

Where are those shastras? Bring them here! I'll burn those unjust shastras that prescribe one justice for men and another for women, and in that very fire I'll throw you in and roast you too, traitor!
Bama! Not only have you become a prostitute, you're also speaking fast to hide it!

Yes, I am a prostitute. But I will not forget that I am your former lover! Why did I become a prostitute? To spend my time in amusement and entertainment? No. No, not for that. To make you prey to the flames rising from my burning heart! To make you a feast for the spear-point sharpened in the fire of agony! Bama assumed the guise of a courtesan not to earn money, but to live. And I live not because I fear death, but to take revenge on the vile Paranthaman! Revenge for revenge! Here—Bama's task is finished. Her purpose has been fulfilled! Fulfilled!
(Saying this, she takes out a knife and moves to stab him; Paranthaman escapes.)
(Scene ends.)
